# TLS-Anvil expected failures, keyed <class path below ...suite.tests>.<TestMethod>.
# Regenerated by tests/tlsanvil/run.sh --update-baseline; document every change in git.
#
# Snapshot 2026-09-15 (TLS-Anvil 1.5.x image of 2026-06-29, -strength 1,
# tls_blocking_server with the P-256 certificate): 181/218 passed, 37 failed
# (35 PARTIALLY_FAILED, 2 FULLY_FAILED), 219 disabled for features we
# do not offer (TLS 1.0/1.1, SSL 3, DTLS, PSK-only, RSA key exchange, CBC,
# client tests). Counted with the fixed summarize.py key (full class path):
# the 2026-09-14 snapshot, "152/199 passed, 47 failed" under the old bare-class
# key, is 165/218 passed, 53 failed under this one. Every remaining entry is a
# documented decision, none an open bug:
#
#  A. INTENTIONAL (RFC 8422 5.3): every TLS 1.2 test loses the parameter
#     combinations where the client lists ECDH_X25519 but not SECP256R1 in
#     supported_groups. "If the client has used a Supported Elliptic Curves
#     Extension, the public key in the server's certificate MUST respect the
#     client's choice of elliptic curves", so with a P-256 certificate we
#     answer handshake_failure; TLS-Anvil expects a ServerHello. Covers every
#     PARTIALLY_FAILED server.tls12.* and both.tls12.* entry below (the P-256
#     half of each passes), and the X25519 half of
#     SignatureAlgorithms.ecdsaNoSignatureAlgorithmsExtension.
#  B. INTENTIONAL (RFC 9155): server.tls12.rfc5246.SignatureAlgorithms.
#     ecdsaNoSignatureAlgorithmsExtension expects SHA-1 when the client sends
#     no signature_algorithms extension (RFC 5246 7.4.1.4.1 default); we sign
#     with SHA-256. Same call as the tlsfuzzer chacha20 "Chacha20 in TLS1.1"
#     exclusion.
#  C. INTENTIONAL (RFC 8446 4.6.3): both.tls13.rfc8446.KeyUpdate.
#     respondsWithValidKeyUpdate sends KeyUpdate(update_requested) and waits
#     for our KeyUpdate without sending any application data. The RFC
#     requires the reply "prior to sending its next application data record",
#     and we send it exactly then, because BoringSSL's KeyUpdate-Requested*
#     tests reject a KeyUpdate delivered on its own as unsolicited (see the
#     comment at Key_Update_Pending in sparktls-server-tls13.adb and the
#     keyupdate exclusions in tests/protocol/run.sh). Under that timing this
#     test cannot pass. The 2026-09-14 snapshot recorded it as passing because
#     that run used the short-lived immediate-reply build, reverted the same
#     evening for BoGo parity.
#
# Fixed 2026-09-15 (17 entries left the list): strict ClientHello extension
# parsing (a walker that stops on a malformed element now answers
# decode_error; inner list lengths must tile psk_key_exchange_modes,
# supported_versions, ec_point_formats and the pre_shared_key identities;
# renegotiation_info must be 1 + n bytes with n = 0; extended_master_secret,
# encrypt_then_mac and early_data must be empty), an undefined record type
# or a second ChangeCipherSpec after the TLS 1.2 handshake now gets
# unexpected_message instead of silence, and Close_Notify no longer sends a
# second close_notify from Closing (AlertProtocol.closeNotify saw two alerts;
# its remaining failures are family A).
both.tls12.rfc5246.Fragmentation.sendZeroLengthApplicationRecord
both.tls12.rfc5246.HappyFlow.happyFlow
both.tls13.rfc8446.KeyUpdate.respondsWithValidKeyUpdate
